thread:
customer-ops: Hey team — after we flipped to our private connectivity (interface endpoint -> NLB) we're seeing intermittent 502s and spikes in TLS handshake time from prod subnets. Only affects calls to the Redwood API. Screenshot/logs attached. Anyone seen TLS/SNI weirdness with private setups?

maria: Hi — can you share the VPC ID + endpoint id? Quick checklist: endpoint ENIs in expected AZs, SG egress open, route table ok, and whether you enabled Private DNS for the endpoint. Also, did you CNAME traffic to the NLB or use the vpce DNS? :thinking:

customer-ops: VPC vpc-03f6a9b2, endpoint vpce-0a12b3c4, service com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-0a1b2c3d. We registered a custom CNAME so api.company.internal -> nlb-123.elb.amazonaws.com. Private DNS for the aws vpce was NOT enabled. SG is pretty permissive outbound 0.0.0.0/0:443, inbound limited to our app subnets.

sean: That CNAME + not using Private DNS is a red flag. Interface endpoints expect either private DNS (which maps the AWS service name to the endpoint ENIs) or you should hit the NLB directly but then SNI/Host header must match the cert the NLB presents. Can you run an openssl s_client from a host in the same subnet and paste the output? e.g.:

```
openssl s_client -connect nlb-123.elb.amazonaws.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com
```

customer-ops: Pasted output: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 /C=US/O=Amazon/OU=Server CA/CN=Amazon Root CA 1
verify return:1
subject=/CN=redwood-inference.prod
---
SSL handshake has read 3123 bytes and written 389 bytes
---
```

maria: Cert CN=redwood-inference.prod — so if your Host header or SNI is `api.company.internal` the backend may reject or the proxy could return 502. Also some corporate DNS setups rewrite CNAMEs (split-horizon) which can cause the client to hit the NLB with a mismatched SNI.

eng-oncall: Also check that your VPC resolver isn't resolving the api hostname to the NLB public IP instead of the vpce ENIs. From an instance in the app subnet run:

```
dig +short api.company.internal
traceroute -n api.company.internal
curl -v "https://api.company.internal/health" -H "Host: api.redwood.example.com"
```

customer-ops: dig returns `10.2.5.12` (one of the ENI IPs) sometimes, but other times it returns the NLB public IP 3.121.45.67. That matches the flakiness. We have split-horizon rules and a conditional forwarder to our onprem resolver.

sean: There you go — DNS split-horizon + custom CNAME + missing Private DNS is likely the cause. When the client resolves to the public NLB IP but sends SNI/Host matching the private cert or vpce domain, the connection can fail or return 502 depending on the path. Two options: enable Private DNS on the VPC endpoint so the AWS service domain maps to the endpoint ENIs, or update your DNS forwarder to prefer VPC resolver for that FQDN.

maria: Quick mitigation: for your prod subnets, add a VPC resolver rule that forwards api.company.internal to the VPC (or add a static A record pointing to the ENI) until DNS is cleaned up. Also confirm security group on the endpoint ENIs allows inbound from your app subnets. Remember: interface endpoints are ENIs — SGs are stateful but you still need to permit inbound traffic from callers.

customer-ops: Ok will try enabling Private DNS. One question: we use NACLs with restrictive ephemeral ports policy — could that cause TLS handshake timeouts?

eng-oncall: Yes — if NACL blocks ephemeral (>1024) return ports you can see broken TLS flows. Ensure ephemeral port range allowed in the NACLs for both directions or avoid NACL state gaps for the subnets hosting the ENIs. Also validate route tables: make sure there's no NAT hairpin or asymmetric route that sends reply to NATGW causing source IP changes — that breaks TLS session affinity to the NLB.

customer-ops: Running tcpdump now and I'll share pcap. Command used: `sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/redwood.pcap host 3.121.45.67 and port 443`

sean: Thanks — if you can share pcap + dig/curl outputs we can correlate SNI and IPs. If you need a short-term workaround: switch the app to call the hosted public API (with proper ACL) or set host header to the cert CN (api.redwood.prod) while DNS is fixed. Both are temporary.

maria: Also creating a support case on our side to check upstream NLB cert mapping and if our ALB/NLB is seeing mismatched hostnames. Can you confirm whether the NLB is doing TLS passthrough or TLS termination at targets? (we expect passthrough for this setup)

support-bot: Created ticket INC-7845 and linked logs — assigned to eng-infra. :white_check_mark:

customer-ops: Uploaded pcap + dig/curl outputs to the ticket. Enabling Private DNS now, will report back in ~10m. Thanks for the triage so far :bow:
